Per-clause scoring of the two repro predicates for issue #3872
against every capture that uses the repro command list.
A '.' means the clause did not match; 'X' means it did.

captures, in column order:
  main   out-main-debug.txt               the repro, ground truth -- expect ALL match
  ce     variant-ce-main-debug.txt        the source published to Compiler Explorer -- the link is not an untested variant: expect ALL match
  nosr   variant-nosr-main-debug.txt      same pipeline, arbitrary RATE semantic -- control: the disputed semantic is absent
  diag   variant-diagnosed-main-debug.txt same semantic in NA cells of the same stages -- control: DXC does diagnose this, these command lines reach it
  gsvin  variant-gsvin-main-debug--match-gsvin.txt the separate gs_6_4 open-question probe -- control: the repro predicate is scoped to its own five compiles
  1.4    out-v1.4.1907.txt                the repro, oldest release -- scored no-repro by match.json; this says which clause
  1.5    out-v1.5.2010.txt                the repro, next release -- scored repro
  1.6    out-v1.6.2104.txt                the repro, release nearest the report -- scored repro
  1.9    out-v1.9.2607.txt                the repro, newest release -- scored repro

Read the 1.4 column against the 1.5 column: the acceptance clauses hold in both.
